title: Friuli-Venezia Giulia Pays More at the Pump as a Six-Day Climb Continues
dek: Self-service Benzina and Gasolio in the northeast are both running above the national average, and the region's prices have risen every day for nearly a week straight.
body: Today's spotlight region is Friuli-Venezia Giulia, where self-service Benzina sits at €2.018/L and self-service Gasolio at €2.146/L. Both are above the national self-service averages of €2.005/L for Benzina and €2.123/L for Gasolio — a gap of about 1.3 cents on petrol and 2.4 cents on diesel, meaning drivers filling up in the region are paying a modest but real premium compared to the rest of Italy.

The trend has been quietly upward all week: Benzina has climbed from €2.008/L on August 11th to today's €2.018/L, and Gasolio has moved from €2.131/L to €2.146/L over the same stretch — six straight days of gains for both fuels. Of the region's 520 registered stations, 469 reported prices today, a 90% reporting rate that's held steady and points to an active, well-monitored local network.

Numbers like these — a full week of daily, region-by-region price history, refreshed automatically every morning — would be a slog to maintain by hand in a spreadsheet. Fuel Dashboard pulls the official MIMIT data, recomputes every regional and national figure, and rebuilds itself each day without anyone touching a keyboard, all built with Claude Code.

Fuel Dashboard is a free, self-updating site that tracks Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano prices across all 20 Italian regions, pulling directly from the official MIMIT feed every day. No manual spreadsheet, no copy-pasting numbers — just fresh, structured pricing data you can actually browse. Take a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

This is also a small case study in what's now possible with AI coding tools. The entire pipeline — data ingestion, regional rotation logic, the article you're reading the caption for, and the site deployment — runs through Claude Code instead of a hand-maintained Excel file. What used to be a recurring manual chore is now a system that reports on itself, every single morning.
